headline: Taiwan indicts ex-TSMC manager for stealing chip secrets for China, seeking 7 years
summary: This marks the first case under Taiwan's National Security Act involving an alleged attempt to leak its most sensitive chip technologies to China, though the transfer was reportedly thwarted.
details: Taiwanese prosecutors have indicted a former TSMC deputy manager, Chen, for allegedly copying 21 confidential documents, some covering national core technologies. Prosecutors are seeking up to seven years in prison for Chen, who has been detained since May, for intending to use these secrets in China.

The alleged transfer of these sensitive chip technologies never occurred. TSMC's internal monitoring systems flagged irregularities, and the company reportedly recovered all improperly copied documents after its own investigation. Despite the failed attempt, prosecutors describe this as the first case of its kind under Taiwan's National Security Act.

Chen was discovered during an investigation into a separate Chinese espionage network, allegedly led by Hong Kong national Ding Xiaohu. Investigators claim Ding, acting on instructions from a Chinese military commission, recruited agents to collect intelligence on Taiwan's critical technologies.

Between May 2023 and February 2024, Chen and Ding allegedly collaborated to establish CSMAC, a semiconductor materials analysis company in China. Chen drafted proposals, including a 'Blue Ocean Plan' to recruit Taiwanese chip industry workers, and took TSMC documents home for this purpose.

This case is distinct from previous TSMC trade secret disputes, which typically involved employees moving to other chip companies. The current indictment highlights allegations of state-directed recruitment and industrial espionage linked to a foreign military entity.

Taiwan's National Security Act, enacted in 2022, criminalizes the copying or disclosure of trade secrets related to designated national core technologies, including chipmaking processes more advanced than 14nm. Previous charges under this act involved alleged attempts to leak 2nm process data.
